title: Impact of Surprise Tariff Announcements on Industry Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

We will use an Event Study approach to analyze the impact of surprise tariff announcements on industry returns. This method is suitable because it allows us to examine the stock returns around a specific event (the tariff announcement) and isolate the effect of the event from other market factors.

The key assumption in this approach is that the stock returns are not affected by the event before the announcement (i.e., the returns are normal or expected). After the announcement, we expect to see a deviation from the normal returns, which we can attribute to the impact of the event.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(plm)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s66_data.csv")

# Calculate the abnormal returns (AR) by subtracting the market returns
data$ar <- data$ret - data$mkt_ret

# Create a factor for event days
data$event_day_factor <- factor(data$event_day)

# Define the event window (-10 to 0) and the estimation window (-11 to -1)
event_window <- -10:0
estimation_window <- -11:-1

# Subset the data for the estimation and event windows
estimation_data <- subset(data, event_day %in% estimation_window)
event_data <- subset(data, event_day %in% event_window)

# Calculate the mean abnormal return for the estimation window
mean_ar <- aggregate(ar ~ event_day_factor, data = estimation_data, FUN = mean)

# Merge the mean AR with the event data
event_data <- merge(event_data, mean_ar, by = "event_day_factor")

# Calculate the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for the event window
event_data$car <- rowSums(event_data$ar - event_data$ar.x)

# Run a fixed effects regression to estimate the impact of the event on CAR
fe_model <- plm(car ~ event_day_factor, data = event_data, model = "within")

# Print the coefficient for the event day
coef(summary(fe_model))

# Robustness check: Cluster-robust standard errors
coeftest(fe_model, vcovHC(fe_model, type = "HC1"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

We expect the coefficient for the event day (day 0) to be negative and statistically significant. This is because surprise tariff announcements are likely to have a negative impact on the stock returns of industries exposed to international trade, as they introduce uncertainty and potential costs associated with trade. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the specific industries and companies involved, but we expect a noticeable decline in returns around the event day.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Leverage the event-day variation around the surprise announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The surprise tariff announcement led to a significant decrease in CAR for exposed industries.
